### 2.1 English (main) — 3263 characters (limit 5000)

```text
Reference ranges in a PDF. Formulas in a chat. A calculator in another app.
One app for the lab specialist, the teacher and the student — in Uzbek, Russian and English. A two-minute tour.

In this video:
• What LabGuide is: a laboratory reference and learning app in Uzbek, Russian and English. Core content works offline and without an account, and the app’s own privacy text says no ads, analytics or tracking. The home screen follows the role you choose.
• For the laboratory specialist: test cards with units, guideline thresholds and a cited source for each claim; calculators that work only from your own values; Levey–Jennings quality control with Westgard rules; a calibration record; a differential counter; the instrument catalog and the atlases; in Uzbekistan, practice for the category assessment; records that stay on your phone.
• For the teacher: lecture slides and practical protocols for a big screen, offline too; a class that students join with a QR or a short code (sign-in needed); a lecture test where questions can differ per student; results by student and the hardest questions.
• For the student: learning from slides by topic, five new questions a day, topic quizzes with every answer explained, timed practice exams that work offline with a mistakes review, and a test from your teacher on the home screen.

Chapters
0:00 Scattered lab knowledge
0:10 What LabGuide is, and your role
0:26 For the laboratory specialist
1:07 For the teacher
1:27 For the student

What LabGuide does today:
• Role changes the home screen and its shortcuts; the knowledge base is the same for every role.
• Classes need an account and a connection; the rest of the core content works without one.
• The category-assessment practice appears for the specialist and teacher roles, for Uzbek-language or Uzbekistan-region users, not for the student role.

Good to know:
• Class screens (class code, QR, test, results, the student’s home) use demo data from the app’s own test server; control, calibration and count values are illustrative.
• The video does not interpret any value and shows no reference intervals: the app gives guideline thresholds on some cards and says your laboratory’s intervals decide.
• Test-card thresholds and all other app content are under expert review.
• No numbers are claimed for how much content the app holds.

LabGuide is a clinical-laboratory companion app for lab professionals and students (English, Russian, Uzbek). It is a learning and reference tool: it does not diagnose or interpret patient results. Works offline and without an account.
Get the app: [[LINK_APP_STORE]] · [[LINK_PLAY]]

Illustrative data — not patient results.
Educational use, not medical advice.
English synthetic narration (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0); English subtitles.
Expert review pending: this content has not yet been reviewed by a laboratory specialist.

Credits
• Narration: AI text-to-speech, Kokoro-82M v1.0 (Apache-2.0), voice af_heart, run with kokoro-onnx (MIT).
• Fonts: Inter and Instrument Serif, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
• Illustrations, schematics, animation and app screens: LabGuide (own work). No third-party photographs, stock footage, music or logos.
• Made with Remotion and FFmpeg.

#LabGuide #LabSpecialist #MedicalTeacher
```

* Imagery: original schematics (`docs/SCHEMATICS_PROVENANCE.md`) and real app screens; no micrographs or photographs.
* Music: none. Logo: owner's app icon (`assets/images/logo_mark_large.png`).

## 10. End screen / CTA suggestion

* YouTube end screen (last ~7–20 s): subscribe + the next video in the SAME language edition (`qc`, `calculators`) + the playlist `[[LINK_PLAYLIST]]`. Place elements so they do not cover the end card's path pill or disclosure notices (check against the final scene).
* Description and pinned comment carry the store links (`[[LINK_APP_STORE]]`, `[[LINK_PLAY]]`); the video itself shows only the in-app path, no URL and no price.
* Instagram: link in bio (`[[LINK_BIO]]`); ask viewers to save/share, not to "download now".

## 11. Safe-content notes

* No patient data, names or real results anywhere. All numbers on screen are illustrative and labelled so.
* No third-party logo, brand name, stock footage or music. The only logo is the owner's app icon.
* Do not call the voice "natural", "professional" or "human": it is synthetic and nobody has listened to it yet.
* Do not call the content "approved", "verified", "certified" or "clinically validated": expert review is pending.
* No diagnosis, treatment, dosing or "normal range" statement. Reference ranges come from the user's laboratory.
* Do not answer individual medical questions in comments; point to the user's laboratory SOP, the reagent IFU and the clinician.
* No price, discount, product id or availability date in any text (docs/DECISIONS.md D-77/D-78: prices live in the stores).
* Check the platform's own disclosure setting for AI-generated / synthetic voice before posting (NEEDS_OWNER_CHECK: the rules change; the kit already states the voice is synthetic in the text).
* Audience: not made for kids. Category: Education. Comments: moderate; hide spam and requests for medical advice.
